summary: Feed s144_double to NDR is degraded: 19.8% duplicate packets and 91.8% encrypted bytes (above 90% tolerance) reduce detection coverage. No packet drops, one-way, VLAN or overload issues detected.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding the same packets twice - typically aggregating the same SPAN/TAP stream from two ingress ports or a SPAN + TAP overlap without deduplication. 540 of 2731 packets (19.8%) are exact duplicates, well above 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes CPU/storage on duplicate flows, inflates flow counts and alerts, skews behavioral analytics and can cause missed detections due to state confusion.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker-level deduplication to drop identical packets within a short time window before delivery to NDR, restoring single-copy visibility without losing unique traffic.

findings.root_cause: 92% of bytes are TLS-encrypted, exceeding the NDR's 90% tolerance. Traffic is predominantly HTTPS/TLS 1.2-1.3 with no cleartext payload available for inspection.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for deep packet inspection and threat detection; with 91.8% encrypted it is effectively blind to payload content, severely limiting detection coverage to metadata only.

recommended_fix.why: Deploy selective SSL/TLS decryption (or forward keys/logs to NDR) to expose payload for analysis while respecting privacy policy; alternatively tune NDR to focus on encrypted-traffic analytics if decryption is not permitted.
